title: Specified stalk compositors on simultaneous quotient diagrams
statement:
Fix the finite-field coefficient datum [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$. All schemes below have $\ell$ invertible and use compatible small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $\widehat R_T=\lim_n(A_n)_T$. Use $D^b_c(T,R)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], completed pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and point sections $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. For a geometric point $v:s\to T$ and $M\in D^b_c(T,R)$ put $J_v(M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lv^*M)$. Stalks and their representatives $[U,u,a]$ mean [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. For a strict tower $T_\bullet$ of complexes with transitions $t_n$, write $H(T_\bullet)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_T:\prod_nT_n\to\prod_nT_n)[-1]$, $s_T((x_n))=(t_nx_{n+1})$, with degree-$i$ coordinates $(b,a)\in\prod_nT_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nT_n^i$ and differential $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_T)a,da)$.

Let $Z\xrightarrow hY\xrightarrow fX$, $w:s\to Z$, $v:s\to Y$ and $M\in D^b_c(X,R)$ be given. Choose one flat-term K-flat $P\to M$ and its simultaneous quotient tower $P_n$. Use the bounded zigzags and maps $e_{u,P}$ of [lem-trf-bounded-quotient-stalk-realization]. Write $c^{\rm fin}_{f,v,P_n}:(f^*P_n)_v\to(P_n)_{fv}$ for the finite germ comparison [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence], and $\chi_{v,f}:L(fv)^*\to Lv^*Lf^*$ for the compositor specified by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization].

The map $\Gamma(s,\chi_{v,f,M}^{-1}):J_v(Lf^*M)\to J_{fv}(M)$ is represented, under that node's entire-tower counit comparison $\eta_{v,f,M}$ and the $e$ comparisons, by the realization of the strict tower map $c^{\rm fin}_{f,v,P_\bullet}$. More precisely the finite section coordinates satisfy
$$e_{fv,n}=c^{\rm fin}_{f,v,P_n}\,e_{v,f^*P_n}\,\Gamma(s,\chi^{\rm fin}_{v,f,P_n}),$$
so the section-coordinate map is $e_{fv,n}^{-1}c^{\rm fin}_{f,v,P_n}e_{v,f^*P_n}$. These coordinate identifications are comparisons of entire simultaneous quotient diagrams and are independent of representatives and natural for arbitrary integral derived morphisms.

For the iterated pullbacks, the three finite comparison maps and the finite compositor on this same tower obey
$$c^{\rm fin}_{fh,w,P_\bullet}=c^{\rm fin}_{f,hw,P_\bullet}\,c^{\rm fin}_{h,w,f^*P_\bullet}\,(\chi^{\rm fin}_{h,f,P_\bullet})_w.$$
The integral counit identifications carry the last factor to $J_w(\chi_{h,f,M})$ and identify all nested pullbacks with these towers. The identity comparison is the identity tower map, and its integral unit identification at $s$ is $J_{\mathrm{id}}(N)=\operatorname{Fib}_sN$.

For any $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(k)$ and $\delta=\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)$, put $R_{u,\alpha,n}[U,u',x]=[U,u'\delta,x]$. The square between $c^{\rm fin}_{f,v,P_\bullet}$ and $R_{v,\alpha,\bullet},R_{fv,\alpha,\bullet}$ commutes as a strict tower square, and the specified integral comparisons carry this square to its realized square. On a pullback germ $(U,u',V,\theta,x)$ both routes give $[V,\operatorname{pr}_V\theta u'\delta,x]$. All assertions concern the whole diagram before realization, with the same quotient transitions; agreement of separate reductions is not substituted for them.

proof.text: Obtain I from integralPullbackComparisonRealization. Construct strict finite data T using [lem-trf-strict-stalk-towers]; descend this fixed T using [lem-trf-stalk-tower-descent]. Transport its strict equations along toStrict equality.

Expand the integral compositor. Its inverse cancels the pullback realization in integralNormalized, leaving the section image of eta and the inverse finite compositor. sectionsComposition is exactly the required remaining equality.

For integralIteration first cancel eta in the defining compositor to get its realization square. Counit naturality transports that square through reduction. Naturality of the pullback realization and sections transports the resulting counit square to the nested point-fibre equation. All finite maps are the given entire-system maps.

Expand the integral unit. Cancel the completeness unit with its inverse and the finite system unit with its inverse; what remains is integralNormalized at the identity point. Package these three proved equations with the strict equations, descent laws and quotient compatibility.

proof_origin.place: Strict finite diagrams and normalized Roos descent separated; integral compositor, iteration and unit proved explicitly by categorical cancellation and counit naturality in Lean.
